newsitem.title: THAILAND: New Thai polls boosts baht sentiment.
newsitem.headline: New Thai polls boosts baht sentiment.

text.p: Pressure on the Thai baht has eased and foreign investor confidence in the currency is rising following the news that a new government will rule the country after November 17 polls, dealers said on Monday.

"Many people in the market were long on U.S. dollars before the news. Now that the news is here they have reversed positions quite a bit," one currency dealer at Hong Kong-based Peregrine Fixed Income Ltd told Reuters.

Investors were prepared to return to the baht because of its high yields when compared with those of other regional currencies. For example, six-month interest rates on the baht yield around 10 percent.
Outgoing premier Banharn Silpa-archa, whose administration has been blamed for Thailand's recent economic woes such as slower growth and sagging exports, announced the election last Friday.
"Before that they (foreign investors) did not feel comfortable with his existing government. Now after the dissolution they are feeling more comfortable," the Hong Kong-based dealer said.
